pattern.name: Web Worker Communication
pattern.description: Use dedicated Web Worker for embedding generation to avoid UI blocking. Main thread sends note content, worker returns vector.
pattern.flow: 1. Note saved in useNoteStore.updateNote() 2. Debounce 500ms (avoid spam during typing) 3. Post message to embedding.worker.ts with { noteId, content } 4. Worker loads Transformers.js pipeline (singleton) 5. Worker generates embedding and posts back { noteId, vector } 6. Main thread calls indexNote() with vector 7. Update NoteRecord.isIndexed = true, indexedAt = Date.now()

technical_notes.note: EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE: src/lib/rag/orama-index.ts already has createIndex, indexDocument, removeFromIndex, searchIndex, saveIndex. Do NOT duplicate. Story 26.2 should add note-specific schema and wrapper functions.
WEB WORKER SINGLETON: Transformers.js model loading is expensive (~90MB). Use singleton pattern in worker to load model once and reuse. Progress callbacks can update UI via postMessage.
CHUNKING: For long notes, chunk content before embedding (use existing chunkContent() from orama-index.ts). Each chunk gets a separate embedding.
INDEX KEY: Use "notes-{projectId}" as index ID to separate from source documents. This allows unified search across sources AND notes.
DEBOUNCE: Don't trigger embedding on every keystroke. Wait 500ms after last change (same debounce as auto-save). Can share the debounce logic.
FALLBACK: If embedding fails after retries, note is still searchable via BM25 keyword matching (Orama hybrid search handles this automatically).
